notes:
Account summary: Copper Lily builds a product analytics + in-app help layer for mid-market SaaS apps. Started on Redwood hosted API to validate inference quality; impressed with model outputs but cost at scale was primary blocker. Evaluating Dedicated to hit unit cost targets and guarantee latency for live support flows.

POC highlights / quotes:
- 'Hosted output quality is solid; ROI hinges on 2x cost reduction vs hosted or reliable reserved capacity.' - Head of Product
- CFO: 'Need predictable spend. We can commit to a 12-month ramp if pricing aligns and burst protection exists.'

Technical constraints / preferences:
- Primary workloads: conversational support (low 120-300 token responses), embeddings for semantic search, offline reranking for batch jobs.
- Latency targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms for chat in NA; embeddings throughput target 25k/day with 6hr windows for batch reindexing.
- Model preference: available open LLMs (quantized Llama-family), ability to route to cheaper quantized variant for non-critical workloads.
- Needs KMS integration, SSO (SAML), SOC2 compliance attestation, audit logs, and ability to restrict EU customer vectors to EU region.

Commercial posture:
pricing_notes:
Negotiation points captured after commercial sync:
- Proposed committed baseline: Equivalent of 2x A100-class GPUs reserved (approx 1,800 GPU-hours/month) for 12 months at discounted rate.
- Ramp schedule proposed by customer: Q1 start at 25% of committed throughput, Q2 50%, Q3 75%, Q4 100% to align with new product release.
- Burst allowance: 50% additional capacity for short windows (spike protection) included in first 6 months, then evaluated.
- Overage pricing: initially proposed at 1.5x committed rate; customer pushing for 1.25x cap and quarterly reconciliation.
- Ramp credit: ask for partial credit during ramp quarters (apply unused committed hours as credit vs overage in first 6 months).
- SLA ask: 99.9% uptime with response-time SLOs; legal seeking explicit remedy caps.
- Pricing sensitivity: CFO target <= $25k/mo in Year 1; AE has counter-proposal with blended rate ~$28k/mo assuming 12-mo commit + modest ramp credits.
- Next commercial step: draft MSA update with ramp credits + overage cap and finalize committed GPU-hours figure.
commercial_summary: Current state: deep evaluation -> procurement. Customer prefers dedicated for predictable unit economics and routing controls. Main negotiation levers: committed hours, ramp credits, burst band, overage multiplier, SLA language. Legal + Finance engaged; timeline to commit if MSA and pricing acceptable by 2026-06.
